To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
recombinant Newcastle disease virus (rNDV) with increased virulence is more efficient in oncolytic therapy of pancreatic adenocarcinaoma than rNDV expressing type I interferon or an IFN antagonist.

recombinant NDV expressing an interferon protein (rND-hIFNβ) or an interferon antagonist (rND-NS1) have oncolytic efficacy against pancreatic adenocarcinaoma cells in vitro, but that a more virulent rNDV is needed for in vivo efficacy in mice.
lentogenic NDV expressing IFNβ or NS1 proteins have an oncolyctic effect, but that the mesogenic NDV strain is the most promising NDV for the treatment of human pancreatic cancer.

the development of recombinant Newcastle disease virus (rNDV) as an oncolytic agent against pancreatic cancer.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the oncolytic efficacy of rNDV is dependent on the virulence of the virus and the expression of additional proteins does not hamper virus oncolytic efficacy.
rNDV-F1aa, rNDV-ΔM, rNDV-F2aa, rND-VF2aa, rNNDV-F3, rNDV-hF2aa, and rNDV-hΔM are all promising candidates for oncolytic virotherapy of pancreatic cancer.

the oncolytic efficacy of rNDV is enhanced by increasing virulence of the virus, while the expression of additional proteins does not hamper virus oncolytic effects, and that the production of type I interferon is not necessarily detrimental to oncolytic efficacy, as long as the virus is virulent enough to overcome this antiviral effect.
The main takeaway from our work is that
recombinant Newcastle disease virus can be engineered for the treatment of human pancreatic cancer.

lentogenic NDV strains expressing IFNβ are able to induce a strong antiviral response, which can be blocked by expressing an IFN antagonist, and that mesogenic NDVs are more potent than their lentogenic counterparts.
rNDV-F1aa and rNDV-F2aa, which are mesogenic and highly virulent, might be more effective than rNDV-F4aa and rNDVF0 in treating pancreatic cancer.
